items.title: Howard Mandel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003

ctx.x: I think the consumer guide aspect of jazz journalism is valuable if it functions in that way. I like to be a little bit ahead of my readers. I hope I can suggest things to them that they haven’t though of before. I mean I want to be — not always provocative or inspiring but I want to be more insightful. I have a lot of experience listening. That’s what I try to do seriously for a living so I hope I can bring something to them they haven’t thought of before. of our vast experience. The networking aspect, the Jazz Journalists Association started in ’85 at a meeting in Chicago that brought together writers and broadcasters. I think it was sponsored by the NEA. And we decided that we should have some sort of organization, mostly just for networking purposes. So if we go to a city that we’re not familiar with for a festival we’ve got somebody to go out to dinner with. And it’s worked very well that way. know I think I got a little off there. But there are things that jazz journalists do for the art form. We are the historians. We are writing the history in the moment that it’s happening. We’re not waiting until everybody’s dead and then trying to go back and do the research. We’re out there on the front lines, seeing concerts, at the clubs, getting the records and we’re telling you what’s happening now.
